criteria.header_validated: Check the magic prefix plus the fixed header structure of each binary format: sane lengths within the file, nonzero dimensions and counts, and valid version and type codes. No checksums, no decompression, no pixel decode. Truncated or garbled files fail the build with a precise signature error instead of reaching browsers as corrupt bytes.
criteria.magic_only: Check only the leading magic bytes of each binary format. The adapter stays tiny; files with a valid prefix but corrupt bodies still emit and serve, leaving browsers to reject them. Build-time detection covers gross mismatches such as a text file renamed to .png.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot fix the signature depth, or neither depth keeps the required contracts.

binary_signature_depth.instructions: Fix how deeply the compiler validates binary asset signatures: leading magic bytes alone, or magic plus fixed header structure without checksums or decoding. Use common and topics.binary_signature_depth.

criteria.json_bytes: Accept any well-formed UTF-8 file as .json and serve it as application/json. Parsing stays the browser's job; a malformed document is served honestly as data rather than rejected at build time.
criteria.json_must_parse: Reject a .json asset whose bytes do not parse as JSON, treating the grammar as the format signature. Malformed documents fail the build; every served .json asset parses.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot fix .json policy, or neither policy keeps the required contracts.

json_policy.instructions: Fix whether .json assets must parse at build time or may serve any UTF-8 text. Use common and topics.json_policy.

criteria.caller_only: Resolve each name in the manifest of the project that holds the calling source file. Dependency assets stay usable only through callee code that returns html::url values; bare names never cross project boundaries. One manifest per call, no precedence or conflict rules.
criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot fix the ownership scope, or neither scope keeps the required contracts.
criteria.root_union: Resolve each name against the root manifest plus every transitive dependency manifest, with a fixed precedence order and a conflict rule for names declared twice. Bare names cross boundaries; sharing needs no wrapper functions.

ownership_scope.instructions: Fix which manifests an asset::url name resolves against: the caller's own project manifest alone, or the root plus transitive dependency manifests with precedence. Use common and topics.ownership_scope.

criteria.review_needed: The evidence cannot fix the reason vocabulary, or neither vocabulary keeps the required contracts.
criteria.single_missing: Report every unresolvable name with the single reason missing. Callers match one reason; where the name went wrong stays invisible.
criteria.specific_taxonomy: Report an unknown name as missing and a name declared only in another project as unowned. Callers can tell a typo from a boundary error.

reason_vocabulary.instructions: Fix the invalid_url reason vocabulary for unresolvable asset names: one reason for every case, or distinct reasons for unknown versus foreign names. Use common and topics.reason_vocabulary.

fixed_constraints: Compilation rule: each Can operation becomes its equivalent native JavaScript/Bun operation; adapters appear solely to uphold Can contracts and immutability. There are no external users, so legacy syntax, ABI, layouts, and goldens deserve no compatibility effort; keep the compiler simple wherever semantics survive.

P11 authority: the distribution embeds upstream HTMX 2.0.10 bytes verified against sha384-H5SrcfygHmAuTDZphMHqBJLc3FhssKjG7w/CeCpFReSfwBWDTKpkzPP8c+cLsK+V, served at /__can/assets/htmx-2.0.10.min.js with the JavaScript media type, immutable cache headers, and an ETag. htmx-config fixes allowEval=false, allowScriptTags=false, selfRequestsOnly=true, with 204 as no-swap, 422 as swap, and other errors as no-swap. Project routes cannot shadow /__can/.

Project assets are manifest build inputs hashed by the compiler, served at /__can/project/<digest>/<name> via native Bun.file with fixed media types, nosniff, ETag, and immutable caching. The allowlist is .css .png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .avif .ico .woff .woff2 .txt .json .csv. JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, SVG/XML, WebAssembly, source maps, and unknown extensions are rejected, as are mismatched signatures. Digests are sha256 hex of the bytes.

Catalogue authority: asset::url(static str name) -> html::url emits html::invalid_url, runs for real under assertions, and resolves a declared asset name at compile time. Existing invalid_url reasons are syntax, scheme, authority, and same_origin. Route mounts already require static string literals at check time, with malformed literals rejected by the checker rather than at runtime.

Pipeline shape: per-project manifests map asset names to confined normalized paths; project snapshot hashes bytes and fails the build on unreadable files, unsafe names, rejected extensions, or bad signatures. The checker resolves each static name against manifest ownership and embeds either the computed URL or a domain-failure reason; the runtime mints html::url provenance or reports the reason. Served files come only from a compiler-built table; reserved routes precede application routing.
common.purpose: Counsel Can, an immutable compiled tongue, strictly from the evidence packed here. Forgo external lookup, implementation, and discursive answers. Wherever candidates refuse separation, the marked uncertainty outcome applies.

binary_signature_depth.facts: Allowlisted binary formats are PNG, JPEG, GIF, WEBP, AVIF, ICO, WOFF, and WOFF2, each with a documented magic prefix and fixed header fields. Full decodes (CRC checks, decompression, pixel reads) would reimplement codec machinery the toolchain otherwise avoids. Browsers reject corrupt images and fonts without security effect; serving them wastes bytes but executes nothing, since no executable format is allowlisted.

json_policy.facts: Text formats CSS, TXT, and CSV carry no machine-checkable grammar in this toolchain, so all candidates validate them as well-formed UTF-8 only. JSON has a cheap exact grammar check in both Go and Bun. application/json is served bare per RFC 8259 with no charset parameter.

ownership_scope.facts: Every project (root plus each recursive dependency directory) carries its own manifest with its own asset map, and every manifest asset path is confinement-checked at graph load. The checker can map each calling file to its owning project. html::url values are first-class and can cross function and package boundaries; only bare manifest names are in question.

reason_vocabulary.facts: Malformed name literals (traversal, separators, unsafe characters) are check-time rejections under the route-literal precedent, so domain reasons cover only resolution outcomes. A name can be absent everywhere or declared solely in another project. The catalogue fixes the single str reason field with no message channel.
